contracts_produced_or_changed: None. This increment proposes a decision and changes no contract, schema or role.
assumptions: THIS INCREMENT CHANGES NO DECISION AND NO CODE. Three of this package's six blockers are spent, and the two that remain beside G0 had claims that went false.

SPENT: RFC-2026-019 was Proposed and awaiting disposition; it was disposed 2026-09-06. SPENT, and this was the interesting one: RFC-2026-018's status line recorded only that it was disposed while the record had been superseded, and the blocker called that the most dangerous shape a record can have -- one that must not be implemented reading as one that may. That line now carries the supersession explicitly, dated 2026-09-06, with NEVER IN EFFECT and the reason. SPENT: the three §5 lint rules said to be unwritten are written.

AN EARLIER VERSION OF THIS INCREMENT CITED THE WRONG LINE AND AN INDEPENDENT CHECK FOUND IT. It gave scripts/db/run.mjs:307 for §5's first rule. Line 307 is inside authzLint and belongs to RFC-2026-020's app_authz rule -- a different decision, 670 lines from the rule it was standing in for. The citations are now 976-986, 629-635 and 1003-1013, read at f3d3102, and each is paired with what the rule asserts so a reader whose line has drifted can still find it.

REWRITTEN: "A1 has not seen this RFC". False. evidence/WP-0A-DB-00/a1-rfc-022-measurements-2026-09-08.md:338, authored by /claude/a1_bastion, records that RFC-2026-019 §4/1 holds today, measured. The earlier version of this increment checked whether any evidence file had the RFC as its SUBJECT, found none, and kept the blocker -- but the blocker's sentence was wider than the test run against it. The load-bearing half survives and is kept: measuring that one clause holds is not agreeing with the proposal.

REWRITTEN: "Nothing in the tree implements the decision, deliberately." False in its main clause and true in a part. §5 names FOUR rules and says the fourth cannot be written before a command function exists; three are written and none exists.

amends_without_owning's `recorded_on` IS REMOVED. It named work-packages/WP-0A-A0-002.json as the register holding the amendment record; that register's ownership.amended_by has never carried an entry for this package, so the reference was dangling before this branch, and with `paths` already empty it pointed at no amendment at all.
STATUS IS DELIBERATELY NOT MOVED: this package stays in_progress. Half its blockers went away in one increment, which is the shape most likely to be misread as completion.

security_privacy_cost_impact: None to the code. One security-relevant statement did change meaning: the manifest no longer says the three RFC-2026-019 §5 lint rules are unwritten, because they are written and they are the assertions that keep `authenticator` out of the service roles and keep app_command from owning a table. A reader who believed the old blocker would have thought those negatives were unasserted.
known_limitations: NOTHING PREVENTS THE NEXT STALE SENTENCE. A blocker list is prose and no lint reads English.

LINE NUMBERS DRIFT AND THREE ARE CITED HERE. Each is paired with what the rule asserts, which is the mitigation and not a guarantee -- and one citation in an earlier version of this increment was wrong from the moment it was written, so the pairing is the part a reader should trust.

THE RULE-3 LIST HAS NO COMPLETENESS CHECK. catalog-snapshot.json's security_definer_functions holds one entry and, unlike tenantTableLint, nothing asserts the list is complete in either direction -- so "every SECURITY DEFINER function" is only as strong as the snapshot. Recorded rather than fixed: run.mjs is not this package's file.
HALF THIS PACKAGE'S BLOCKERS WENT AWAY IN ONE INCREMENT. The status is unchanged and this handoff says so twice.
open_risks_or_blockers: Three blockers remain OPEN and are listed in the manifest. This increment closes none of them: it removes ones already discharged elsewhere.
AN A1 REVIEW OF RFC-2026-019 AS A WHOLE DOES NOT EXIST. One clause has been measured by an A1 run; the proposal has not been agreed with, and that is the oldest open item on this package.
rollback_or_forward_fix: ROLLBACK: revert this commit. The manifest returns to six blockers, three describing states that no longer hold and one claiming nothing in the tree implements a decision that is implemented three ways.
recommended_next_work_packages: An A1 review of RFC-2026-019 as a proposal rather than a measurement of one of its clauses.
The command function §5's fourth rule waits on. Until one exists the fourth rule cannot be written, which RFC-2026-019's own status line already says.

A rule tying a blocker that names a decision record to that record's status, if one can be written without reading prose. Four manifests have now been corrected by hand for one class of defect, and two of those corrections were themselves wrong on first attempt.
